overall.summary: Every stated number reproduces (coverage 1.0, exact function preservation, closed forms, all probe values, subgroup counts, shares and AUCs). One reading is refuted: unit 2's 'strongest regime' is not x on b1, c1 and d1 (43 positions, 0.5% of the unit's contribution). Its real strongest regimes (x on b1 and c1, open ends, o on f1/g1) are positions x wins 100% of the time, so the unit does match the game where it matters. Two scope overclaims are weakened: the column-d direction reverses on d5/d6, and unit 7 is called a d3 brake 'rather than a separate idea' when 69% of its contribution is elsewhere.

findings.statement: the strongest regime of this unit is fitted to 43 rows and does not match the game there (x on b1, c1 and d1: model 77%, x wins 28%)
findings.check: unit 2 value and contribution by bottom-row pattern on the training split; outcome vs prediction in the unit's highest-value regimes
findings.evidence: The 77% vs 28% figure for the 43 rows reproduces (unit 2 explains it: 34% without the unit). But those rows are not the unit's strongest regime: their mean unit value is 2.73 (max 3.86), none of the unit's top 100 values falls in them, and they carry 0.5% of its total contribution. Eleven other bottom-row patterns have higher means. Example: x on b1 and c1, a1/d1/e1 empty, o on f1 and g1 (n=150, mean 4.21) has model 93.2% and x wins 150 of 150 (100%). Another, x on b1 and c1 with o on f1 (n=119), has model 85% and outcome 100%. Across the 13266 positions where the unit is on, the mean prediction is 67.7% and the outcome 68.3%. Where the unit is strongest, it matches the game.

findings.statement: Unit 2's strongest regime (x on b1, c1 and d1, 43 positions, o blocking both ends) predicts 77% on average where x wins 28%: the model's reading of that line does not match the game
findings.evidence: The numbers 43 / 77% / 28% reproduce, but calling this 'the strongest regime' is wrong (mean unit value 2.73 vs 4.21 in the top pattern; 0.5% of the unit's contribution). In the unit's actual strongest regimes, x wins 100% of the time, so 'the model's reading of that line does not match the game' holds only in a 43-row corner.

findings.statement: x pieces on the centre column d and on the second and third rows of columns c-e raise x's predicted win chance, and o pieces there lower it
findings.check: counterfactual per square on all 54045 training rows (square set to x / empty / o, mean prediction), observed means, and a probe sweep of d6 on the otherwise empty board
findings.evidence: Holds for d1-d4, c2, c3, e2 and e3. Example: d3 counterfactual x 0.879 vs o 0.318. It reverses at the top of column d. d6: counterfactual x 0.466 vs o 0.826; observed mean prediction 43.5% with x on d6 (n=73) vs 74.0% with o (n=171); probe 32.0% (x) / 61.7% (empty) / 82.7% (o). d5: x 0.624 vs o 0.651. So the statement is true for the lower column only. That covers most positions, since d5/d6 are occupied in about 2% of rows.

findings.statement: x pieces in the lower centre (the centre column d and the second and third rows of columns c-e) raise the prediction and o pieces there lower it
findings.evidence: The parenthesis defines the lower centre as the whole of column d, but d6 and d5 run the other way (d6: x 0.466 vs o 0.826 counterfactual). The rest of the root hypothesis reproduces: sigmoid of the units plus bias -0.589, 0 direct edges, signs (1, 2, 3, 5, 6 positive; 4, 7, 8 negative), 20% / 99% probe, 84% of 12328 (x wins 84%) and 43% of 12531 (x wins 44%).

findings.statement: this unit reads as a brake on the reward for x on d3 rather than as a separate idea about the board
findings.check: share of unit 7's total contribution in the x-on-d3 rows vs the rest
findings.evidence: The probe numbers reproduce: -7.37, -1.28, 4.80; 88% to 99.6%; 92.6% of 3812; -2.17; 6.0% of 3901; 24318. But only 31% of the unit's total contribution (-8255 of -26971) comes from the 3812 positions with x on d3, and 69% comes from the 24318 other positions where it is on (mean value 2.0 there). The brake reading covers a minority of what the unit does. 'Rather than a separate idea' overstates it, although the unread activity is acknowledged.

findings.statement: on in 85.9%; positive output weight; grows with x on d3, d2, c3, e3, f3 and o on c1, d1, e1; probe 2.48/5.80/9.13 and 4.08/1.45; mean contribution 4.34 (3812), 1.05 (3901), 4.05 (4478), 1.31 (4782); AUC 0.902 -> 0.782, largest part
findings.check: independent forward pass, probes, subgroups, ablation
findings.evidence: All reproduce: on 0.8590, output weight +0.876, ablation AUC 0.7820 (largest loss). Note: the 'stacked on top of o' reading is additive in the pre-activation. o on d1 raises the unit whatever is above it (d2 empty: 3.16 vs 2.45 with x on d1). So 'stacked' names the combination that maximises the unit, not a conjunction it computes.

findings.statement: on in 24.5%; adds to win chance; b1, c1, d1 then a1 open it, o on f1/g1 opens it, x above the bottom row and o on a1-d1 close it; probe 0.00/1.35/3.19 with 22%/52%/90%; acts on 99.3% of 6990 and 13.4% of 47055; 43 rows with o on a1 and e1 in all
findings.evidence: All reproduce. Only b6 (+0.037) and f6 (+0.072) of the rows-2-6 weights are positive, so 'x above the bottom row closes it' holds. 'x outnumber o by at least two' equals the query's sum >= 2 (both 6990).

xCentreAboveOBottom.why: A board-evaluation reading (x on rows 2-3 of the centre, o under them on the bottom row) that probes and data confirm. The 'stacked' wording names two additive preferences, not a conjunction.

xBottomLeftRow.why: It detects x with two or more pieces along a1-d1 and open ends, with x to move. In its strongest regimes x wins 100% of the time and the model predicts 85-93%. The blocked 43-row case is a small exception, not its main behaviour.

xCentreThirdRow.why: It opens for x on d3 and c3 (86.3% of x-on-d3 positions vs 12.5% of o-on-d3), a domain-level reading of the third-row centre that the probe confirms.

oBottomCentre.why: It grows with o on c1 and d1 and lowers the score, matching the data (mean prediction 51% with o on both vs 70% with x on both), though unit 1 offsets it on the empty board.

xOnC2.why: A clear gate on x holding c2 (60.5% vs 8.4% active), and x wins 85% where it is on.

xLowColumnD.why: It rewards x owning the low centre column (d2, d1, d3), with a clean d1-by-d2 probe and d2 subgroups.

xHighColumnD.why: The d3 brake reading is real but covers only 31% of the unit's total contribution; the other 69% (24318 positions without x on d3) has no reading.

xRightOCentre.why: The o-on-c2/c3 reading holds but the contrast is modest (-1.08 vs -0.66 mean contribution), and its rise with x on e3/f3 has no reading.
